program: Domestic-violence shelter, advocacy, counseling, crisis response and prevention

nutshell.headline: Our exploratory model estimates $22.70 million per 10 Bay QALYs; this is not a giving recommendation.
nutshell.body: A $100,000 ordinary whole-organization gift produces 0.044061 signed prior-weighted Bay QALYs, or $22,695,319 per 10. Across all modeled beneficiaries, the estimate is $22,460,767 donor cash and $26,728,312 modeled gross resources per 10 QALYs. Observed QALYs and verified marginal capacity remain unknown.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Safety-focused advocacy and practical support may reduce abuse and improve short-term health. External intensive post-shelter advocacy trials provide some support for this pathway.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The external intervention differs from La Casa's mixed services. Additionality, advocacy dose, geography and the finite utility bridge are judgments; a 5%-weight favorable world supplies 86.9% of all-beneficiary expected net benefit.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Establish a priced additional service or preservation plan, its funding counterfactual, unduplicated recipients, advocacy dose and finite health outcomes before recommending a gift.

programSection.body: La Casa de las Madres, EIN 94-2330864, provides emergency shelter, community advocacy and counseling, police-response follow-up, statewide crisis lines, supportive-housing services and prevention. Its 2025 report describes 1,384 Bay Area survivors of all ages receiving direct services.

steps.title: Connect with safety and support
steps.detail: Survivors reach crisis response, shelter, a community office or partner co-locations.

steps.title: Receive appropriate advocacy
steps.detail: Only an assumed adult-eligible fraction receiving an intensive-advocacy-equivalent dose enters the health bridge.

steps.title: Count finite additional benefit
steps.detail: Apply funding additionality and a signed finite QALY effect; other contacts and overlapping programs are not separately added.

programSection.boundary: All FY2025 IRS expense of $4,560,661 is charged. The 1,384 direct-service umbrella is non-additive: 885 community-office users, 815 co-location users, 231 sheltered people, 6,571 shelter service-days, 2,226 police contacts and 6,151 calls/texts are not summed. This retains whole-organization costs while leaving non-advocacy health pathways unquantified, not proven zero.

model.headline: Signed expected Bay cost: $22,695,319 per 10 QALYs
model.body: Compute each joint scenario's signed QALYs, weight health outcomes, then divide the whole gift by the weighted result. Do not average prices or discard harmful worlds.

equation.label: CENTRAL ADVOCACY PATHWAY
equation.expression: QBay = (100000 / 4560661) × 1384 × .70 adult-eligible × .20 full advocacy dose × .15 funding additionality × .05 finite QALY × .98 Bay share
equation.result: Central Bay QALYs = 0.031226; all-beneficiary central donor cost = $31,383,574 per 10 QALYs. The prior-weighted Bay headline is not this central scenario.

inputs.label: Whole annual expense
inputs.basis: No overhead or non-advocacy cost removed. Reported $95,586 in-kind input is not assumed included in IRS expense or mechanically added.

inputs.label: Broad direct-service umbrella
inputs.confidence: Organization-reported, not a verified unique-dose census
inputs.basis: Mixed ages and services; overlapping outputs are not added.

inputs.label: Adult eligibility and full advocacy dose
inputs.basis: External intensive post-shelter advocacy evidence cannot be assigned to every person, child, call or brief contact.

inputs.label: Funding additionality
inputs.basis: Public funding, other gifts, reserves and operational capacity may replace or constrain a gift's additional services.

inputs.label: Finite QALY bridge
inputs.basis: 1/8 responders × (0.85−0.63) modeled annual utility gap × 2 years = 0.055, rounded down to 0.05. A 24-month abuse endpoint does not establish continuous two-year remission. Advocate-state utility is only 0.65. The 0.15 tail is a wide judgment, not measured benefit; no mortality credit.

inputs.label: Recipient geography
inputs.basis: Annual report supports Bay presence, not exact residence shares. Statewide hotline receives no direct health credit.

inputs.label: Joint scenario weights
inputs.range: Harm / funding-null / evidence-null / cautious / central / favorable
inputs.basis: Null and negative outcomes are retained. Favorable contribution is 86.9% of all-beneficiary weighted net QALYs.

inputs.label: Gross-resource multiplier
inputs.basis: Intended to encompass unreconciled in-kind and unpriced partner inputs. Verified complete gross resource cost remains unavailable.

sensitivity.headline: Negative Bay health outcome
sensitivity.detail: 5% weight; −0.011470 Bay QALYs. Nonpositive outcomes have no positive cost-effectiveness ratio.

sensitivity.headline: Zero additional health
sensitivity.detail: 25% weight; funding additionality zero. Full gift cost remains.

sensitivity.headline: Zero health effect
sensitivity.detail: 20% weight; the transferred advocacy effect is zero.

sensitivity.headline: 0.000341 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 25% weight; low adult eligibility, dose and funding additionality.

sensitivity.headline: 0.031226 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 20% weight; 0.05 finite QALY per full advocacy equivalent. All-beneficiary central price is $31,383,574 per 10.

sensitivity.headline: 0.766096 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 5% weight; 0.15 finite QALY per equivalent. All-beneficiary favorable price is $1,292,264 per 10, not a quoted donation offer.

sensitivity.headline: $171,517,256 per 10 all-beneficiary QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Original-weight favorable contribution is removed without renormalization; this is the saved model diagnostic, not a Bay ratio.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: The finite bridge combines heterogeneous advocacy and state-utility evidence. Duration, response, eligibility and dose are not measured La Casa effects. No mortality, lifetime or separate additive shelter/prevention benefit is credited. Linear gift scaling is an accounting assumption, not verified large-gift absorption capacity.
model.fundingBoundary: No verified marginal funding offer. FY2025 IRS revenue is $5,062,993, surplus $502,332 and net assets $13,476,875; assets are not all current unrestricted cash. A city executed-agreement report lists Verona Hotel support services through June2027, total NTE $1,332,681, supporting 65 housing units. A draft FY2026–27 plan recommends $165,000 for shelter/case management; final executed award was not verified. These are baseline funding records, not prices for additional advocacy. Public funding and private gifts overlap; no entire grant is subtracted from whole expense. Promotional $100 shelter-night examples are not binding marginal prices.

evidence.result: Annual report gives a broad 1,384 Bay survivor umbrella alongside overlapping service counts and self-reported outcomes.
evidence.transfer: Outputs establish delivery, not causal QALYs. Do not sum contacts or interpret success surveys as effects versus a counterfactual.

evidence.population: 278 former shelter residents receiving ten weeks of advocacy or control
evidence.result: Authors report reduced violence and better quality-of-life-related outcomes across two-year follow-up, with 95% retained.
evidence.transfer: An intensive post-shelter intervention is not La Casa's whole portfolio. Present-day dose, adult eligibility and response remain uncertain.

evidence.design: Systematic review of randomized and quasi-randomized advocacy trials
evidence.population: Women experiencing intimate partner abuse in varied settings
evidence.result: Intensive advocacy may improve some short-term quality-of-life and abuse outcomes; evidence is heterogeneous, often low quality, and several outcomes include no benefit.
evidence.transfer: The NNT≈8 at 24 months is not observed QALY gain or proof of two continuous years without abuse. Null and harm priors remain explicit.

evidence.population: Modeled abused and not-abused states, not La Casa participants
evidence.result: Utilities used include 0.63 abused/unidentified, 0.65 seeing an advocate and 0.85 not abused.
evidence.transfer: Combining the 0.22 gap with an advocacy response rate and finite duration is an analyst heuristic; the full gap is not the measured effect of seeing an advocate.

evidence.result: At nine months PTSD improved, but primary quality of life and several re-abuse and mental-health outcomes were null.
evidence.transfer: Different intervention and setting; supports caution rather than supplying a La Casa coefficient.

evidence.design: City executed-agreement reporting and draft funding recommendations
evidence.population: La Casa housing support and shelter programs
evidence.result: Documented Verona support agreement extends through June2027; separate FY2026–27 shelter support is proposed.
evidence.transfer: Distinguish executed baseline agreements from proposals; neither demonstrates gift-triggered additional capacity.

reservations: The modeled result is unfavorable and is not a recommendation to give.
86.9% of all-beneficiary expected net QALYs comes from a 5%-weight favorable prior.
No observed La Casa QALY effect, verified advocacy-dose mix or marginal funding offer was found.
Public funding, other donors and reserves complicate additionality; assets do not establish unrestricted liquid availability.
The two-year health bridge assumes persistence not established by a 24-month outcome measurement.
Bay and SF shares are unmeasured residence priors; all costs are retained even for unquantified services.
In-kind reconciliation and complete external resource costs remain unknown.
excludedBenefits: Separate additive hotline, police-response, shelter, prevention and co-location QALYs
Child and caregiver health effects beyond the modeled adult advocacy pathway
Financial savings, housing value and taxpayer savings as QALYs
